data.description:
## The defect is the INVISIBILITY, not the loss

`.tickets-tracker` lives **inside** the worktree (`<worktree>/.tickets-tracker`). Ticket events
are committed there immediately and auto-pushed to `sync.remote`. When that push is backed up,
retiring the worktree — `git worktree remove`, the retirement step the `/rebar-debug` and
`/rebar-implement` skills both prescribe — **deletes unpushed ticket events permanently**.

That alone would be a bug. What makes it a defect worth its own ticket is that **the loss is
undetectable by the checks an agent would actually run**:

- `rebar show <id>` reads **local** state, so it reports `status: closed` whether or not the
  close ever left the machine. An agent that closes a ticket, confirms with `rebar show`, and
  retires its worktree has done everything the guidance asks and still loses the close.
- A later reader sees a **closed ticket**. The store does not have it. There is no error, no
  warning at retirement time, and no artifact pointing at what went missing.

This is the `sphinxian-agrarian-snake` (`3fce-cccf-d38b-4072`) shape exactly: *a check whose
pass result is indistinguishable from the check never having run*. Here the overloaded signal
is `rebar show` reporting `closed` — identical output for "closed and shared" and "closed into
a directory that is about to be deleted".

## Measured, on bug 84c7-486f (`surprised-convincing-gopher`), 2026-08-21

The close of that bug came within one command of being destroyed. Numbers as observed:

| Observation | Value |
|---|---|
| unpushed ticket commits in the worktree tracker at close time | **138** |
| backlog across successive auto-push attempts | **103 -> 190 -> 194** (growing, not draining) |
| `rebar doctor` | **structurally clean throughout** — 15 findings, all pre-existing link-shape issues on unrelated tickets; locks free |
| `rebar tracker-maintenance --status` | **0 stranded index entries, 0 foreign top-level paths** |
| `rebar show surprised-convincing-gopher` | `status: closed` |

**That last pair is the crux.** Both existing diagnostics reported a healthy store, and the
read command reported a closed ticket, while the close existed **nowhere but a directory about
to be deleted**. Whatever remedy is chosen has to close that gap: today, health checks pass and
reads look right in exactly the state where retirement destroys data.

The loss was caught only by an **ad-hoc** comparison of local vs remote event sets, which is
not a check anything prescribes:

```
        event                 remote   local
        STATUS                  0        1     <- the close
        COMPLETION_VERDICT      0        1     <- the signed verdict
        SIGNATURE               1        2
        LINK                    4        5     <- the caused_by
```

The push was not broken and the store was not corrupt: after a fetch the branch was
`remote-only: 0, local-only: 141` — a clean fast-forward was available and rebar's own
auto-reconcile merge commits were present. The auto-push was simply losing a race against a
busy shared remote. Driving it with further rebar writes eventually reached
`unpushed ticket commits : 0`, after which `STATUS 1/1`, `COMPLETION_VERDICT 1/1`,
`SIGNATURE 2/2`, `LINK 5/5` and divergence 0 both ways were confirmed against a fresh fetch.
**Retirement one minute earlier would have lost all of it.**

Note the exposure is not hypothetical or confined to one session: this is a machine with ~90
live worktrees, and the shared checkout's own tracker showed **14 unpushed** while this ticket
was being filed.

## This is the third instance of one class: tracker-derived state living per-worktree

- `intangible-ladyish-vicuna` (`93a9-66cf-e681-4f49`, **closed**) — compaction trigger sidecars
  were worktree-local rather than store-scoped, so two worktree views of one store each held
  the "one compactor at a time" lock simultaneously.
- `nuclear-calm-heron` (`da68-fc7c-068c-4c53`, **in_progress** — the fix for the enrichment
  drain is described in vicuna as landed, but the ticket is not closed, so treat this as an
  open sibling rather than a second completed repair) — "worktree-local drain lock does not
  serialise a shared store".
- **This ticket** — the tracker's *unpushed event backlog* is worktree-local, and worktree
  retirement is a destructive operation with no awareness of it.

The first two are about **correctness under concurrency**; this one is about **durability under
teardown**. Same root shape — state that belongs to the store is scoped to a worktree — which
is why it is filed as a sibling rather than folded into either.

## Explicitly NOT proposing a design

Several remedies are plausible and they are **not** equivalent in scope, so the choice must be
justified rather than assumed. Recording the options only so the next agent does not have to
rediscover them:

- a **pre-retirement guard** that refuses or warns when the tracker has unpushed commits;
- a **push-drain** on worktree removal;
- a **`rebar doctor` leg** that reports unpushed commits as a finding (today it does not);
- making `rebar show` (or the close path) **surface unshared state** so the read stops being
  ambiguous;
- **relocating the tracker** out of the worktree entirely.

Some of these are restoration; at least one (relocating the tracker) is a substantial
architectural change, and a guard on `git worktree remove` reaches a command rebar does not own
— a portability question, since not every environment retires worktrees the same way, and a
capability whose only trigger is one workflow is not portable. **Do not treat the option list as
a decision.**

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The failure is reproduced deliberately: a ticket event committed to a worktree tracker
      with a non-empty unpushed backlog, the worktree retired, and the event shown absent from
      `sync.remote` while `rebar show` still reported the local status.
- [ ] The chosen remedy is **justified against the alternatives listed above**, with the
      reasoning recorded on this ticket, including an explicit statement of whether it restores
      intended behaviour or adds new capability, and whether it is portable across environments
      that do not use git worktrees.
- [ ] After the change, the state in which retirement destroys data is **detectable by a check
      an agent would actually run** — the specific check named, and shown failing before the fix
      and passing after. `rebar doctor` reporting clean and `tracker-maintenance --status`
      reporting 0 stranded entries while a close is unshared must no longer both be true.
- [ ] A test exercises the unshared-close state, seen RED before the fix.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the full suite stay green.

## Provenance

Found while closing bug `surprised-convincing-gopher` (`84c7-486f-9a13-4c3f`) under
`/rebar-debug`. Not fixed there: that bug is scoped to the `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` table->tree
invariant, and the remedy here is undecided and may be architectural.

Two evidence divergences from that bug's close are recorded here as well, since they bear on
how much its green result should be trusted:

1. Its AC *"the full unit sweep stays green"* was met by **CI, not by a local run** — the host
   sat at load 22-54 from concurrent sessions for the entire session and no local full sweep
   ever completed. Evidence is CI run 32488951833 (green on ubuntu py3.11/3.12/3.13 and macos
   py3.13); the more informative datum is the patchset-1 run, `1 failed, 15169 passed`, whose
   single failure was that change's own comment-hygiene defect.
2. Its AC *"`tests/scripts/test_check_config_ownership_heldout.py` must stay green"* is met in
   final state but **not literally**: removing the ghost rows correctly turned that test RED
   (its fixture selected a helper via `next(iter(KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS))`, which resolved to a
   ghost row), and it required a fixture repair. The divergence was recorded rather than the AC
   reworded, since rewording AC prose would have staled the plan-review attestation.
data.title: Retiring a worktree silently destroys unpushed ticket events, and every existing check reports healthy
